title: Heron's Formula
prerequisites: Area of a triangle as ½ × base × height.
Familiarity with the perimeter of a polygon.

topics.title: Heron's Formula and Its Applications
topics.quick_summary: Heron's formula finds the area of a triangle from its three sides alone, without needing the height.
topics.real_life: A farmer with a triangular field can measure the three boundary lengths with a tape and compute the area exactly — no need to find any perpendicular.

detailed.definition: For a triangle with sides a, b and c and semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c)/2, the area is √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)].
detailed.key_idea: The formula's whole value is that it needs no height. For a scalene triangle, finding a perpendicular height is awkward, while measuring three sides is easy.
detailed.working_principle: Compute s first, then each of the three differences, then multiply and take the square root. Keeping surds in exact form until the last step avoids accumulated rounding error.
applications: Area of a quadrilateral: split it along a diagonal into two triangles and add.
Area of an equilateral triangle of side a is (√3/4)a².
Checking whether a triangle is valid: if any (s − a) is negative, the triangle cannot exist.

points: s = (a + b + c)/2 is the semi-perimeter, half the perimeter.
Useful when the height is unknown or hard to find.
A quadrilateral is handled by splitting it into two triangles along a diagonal.
For a right triangle, the ordinary ½ × base × height is quicker.
mistakes: Using the full perimeter instead of the semi-perimeter.
Forgetting to take the square root at the end.
Rounding intermediate values, which distorts the final answer.
topics.memory_hook: 'Half the perimeter, then s minus each side, multiply all four, square root.'
topics.advanced: Heron's formula can be derived from the cosine rule with some algebra, and Brahmagupta's formula generalises it to cyclic quadrilaterals. Both are special cases of Bretschneider's formula for any quadrilateral.

formulas.name: Heron's Formula
formulas.formula: Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)],  where s = (a + b + c)/2
formulas.variables: a, b, c = the three sides of the triangle, s = semi-perimeter.
formulas.when_to_use: Whenever all three sides are known and the height is not.
formulas.common_mistakes: Using the perimeter instead of the semi-perimeter, or omitting the square root.
formulas.shortcut: If the triangle is right-angled, ½ × base × height is far quicker.

formulas.name: Area of an Equilateral Triangle
formulas.when_to_use: For any equilateral triangle, as a shortcut instead of Heron's formula.
formulas.common_mistakes: Using √3/2 instead of √3/4, which is the height factor, not the area factor.
formulas.shortcut: Height of an equilateral triangle is (√3/2)a.
